distractorExplanations.b: Tender spread is a tender analysis metric, not the cost plan to tender to outturn trajectory the triangle reports.
distractorExplanations.c: Contractor margin is the contractor's internal commercial measure; the triangle tracks the employer's budget through the stages.
distractorExplanations.d: That is external benchmarking of a single cost plan, not tracking of the same budget from cost plan through tender to actual.

options.a: Grade of protection under BS 8102, with installed cost per m² broadly the same for both
options.b: Risk profile, joint detailing, repairability, and warranty approach
options.c: Programme duration only, as joint detailing and warranty terms are the same for both
options.d: Concrete grade and cover, treating both as BS 8102 Type B integral protection

distractorExplanations.a: The BS 8102 grade is set by the intended use of the space; the two systems differ materially in risk, joint detailing, repair and warranty.
distractorExplanations.c: Joint detailing and warranty terms differ between integral waterproof concrete and applied membranes, as does repairability.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses BS 8102 types: an applied membrane is Type A barrier protection, while waterproof concrete is Type B structurally integral.

options.a: A right to terminate for repudiatory breach once payment is 28 days overdue under the HGCRA
options.b: Contractual interest, as HGCRA suspension rights apply to final payment certificates but not interim ones
options.c: Statutory interest and potential suspension rights per HGCRA on qualifying contracts
options.d: Adjudication, since suspension of works requires a court order under the Scheme

distractorExplanations.a: The HGCRA gives a statutory right to suspend after notice, not a termination right triggered by a fixed number of days late.
distractorExplanations.b: Suspension rights under s112 HGCRA apply to any sum due that is not paid in full by the final date, including interim payments.
distractorExplanations.d: Suspension under the HGCRA needs only seven days' written notice, not a court order; adjudication is a separate remedy.

options.a: Upgraded carpet and underlay to the floor, relying on soft finishes for impact sound
options.b: Resilient bars and insulation in the floor void, with flanking junctions left to the party wall package
options.c: Floating deck to Approved Document L standards, with pre-completion sound testing excluded
options.d: Insulation, resilient bars, floating deck, flanking paths, and testing allowance

distractorExplanations.a: Soft coverings alone do not achieve Part E airborne and impact performance in conversions or deal with flanking transmission.
distractorExplanations.b: Flanking paths at junctions are a key acoustic risk and must be costed with the floor build-up, not excluded to another package.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses Part L (energy) with Part E (sound); Part E pre-completion testing is a required allowance on residential conversions.

options.a: Assess exposure, retender packages, and update forecast/cash flow
options.b: Call the main contractor's performance bond for the full replacement cost of the packages
options.c: Hold the forecast at tender value until the administrator confirms the package position
options.d: Instruct the remaining works as a variation priced at the insolvent firm's tender rates

distractorExplanations.b: A main contractor bond covers main contractor default; subcontractor insolvency is first a cost and programme exposure to assess.
distractorExplanations.c: Holding the forecast hides a known risk; the QS should reflect exposure and retender cost in the forecast as soon as it is known.
distractorExplanations.d: Replacement packages rarely hold the failed firm's rates; retendering in a distressed market usually costs more and takes longer.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Supply chain failure triggers retender, cost, and programme reassessment. Value any acceleration cost needed to recover programme.

options.a: Earlier MEP first fix on site, as pods arrive unplumbed for trades to complete in situ
options.b: Parallel manufacture while site works proceed, reducing critical path duration
options.c: A shorter rectification period, since factory-tested pods sit outside the defects regime
options.d: Lower preliminaries through a reduced crane requirement, as pods are positioned by hand

distractorExplanations.a: Pods arrive factory-fitted and pre-plumbed; the benefit is offsite manufacture in parallel with site works, not earlier first fix.
distractorExplanations.c: Pods remain part of the works and are covered by the rectification period; factory testing does not remove them from it.
distractorExplanations.d: Pods are heavy volumetric units usually lifted by crane; the programme gain comes from parallel manufacture, not less lifting.

options.a: Separate monthly reports for each stakeholder, each using its own CPI and FFC definitions
options.b: Monthly cost report with FFC based on certified valuations to date, excluding risk
options.c: Integrated monthly report with definitions consistent across project stakeholders
options.d: Monthly report showing committed cost as the FFC, with cash flow taken from the tender S-curve

distractorExplanations.a: Different definitions per stakeholder make the KPIs non-comparable; the dashboard needs one consistent set of definitions.
distractorExplanations.b: Certified valuations to date are not a forecast; FFC must include committed cost, anticipated changes and risk allowances.
distractorExplanations.d: Committed cost excludes uncommitted works, change and risk, so it is not the FFC; a static tender S-curve is not a live cash flow forecast.

options.a: Standard cantilevered balcony connections, with heat loss offset by the façade insulation
options.b: Thermal break units as a provisional sum, deferring the structural interface to Stage 5
options.c: Insulated balcony soffit cladding only, treating the slab connection as a Part A item
options.d: Structural thermal break details, insulation continuity, and condensation risk mitigation

distractorExplanations.a: Façade insulation cannot offset a continuous slab thermal bridge; a structural thermal break is needed to limit heat loss and condensation.
distractorExplanations.b: The thermal break is a structural design decision for Stage 3/4; deferring it to Stage 5 leaves cost and design risk unresolved.
distractorExplanations.c: Soffit cladding does not break the thermal bridge through the slab; the connection needs a combined structural and thermal detail.

options.a: Application matches site progress, contract rates, variations authorised, and retention deducted
options.b: Application totals reconcile to the cash-flow forecast, with off-site materials paid on request
options.c: Works valued at contract rates, including unauthorised works the contractor states were necessary
options.d: Value of works completed, plus materials ordered from suppliers but not yet delivered to site

distractorExplanations.b: Cash-flow alignment is not verification; off-site materials need contract provisions such as vesting and insurance before payment.
distractorExplanations.c: Only instructed or authorised work is certifiable; unauthorised work needs an instruction or confirmation before it is valued.
distractorExplanations.d: Materials ordered but not delivered are not valued in an interim application unless the contract makes off-site provisions.

options.a: Waterproofing membrane grade only, since both roof types share the same build-up and load
options.b: Growing medium depth, plant species, irrigation, structural loading, and maintenance
options.c: Drainage layer and filter fleece specification, with structural loading and upkeep similar
options.d: Roof pitch, as intensive systems suit pitched roofs while extensive ones need a flat deck

distractorExplanations.a: Intensive roofs carry far deeper substrate and heavier loads than extensive systems; the build-up and loading are not the same.
distractorExplanations.c: Drainage layers differ little; the cost gap comes from substrate depth, planting, irrigation, loading and maintenance.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the pitch rule: extensive systems can go on shallow pitches, while heavy intensive roofs need a flat deck and deep substrate.

options.a: NRM2: Detailed measurement for building works
options.b: CESMM4 without modification for building works
options.c: NRM1: Order of cost estimating and cost planning
options.d: SMM7: Standard Method of Measurement, 7th edition

distractorExplanations.c: NRM1 governs order of cost estimates and elemental cost plans, not the detailed measurement rules for a tender BOQ.
distractorExplanations.d: SMM7 was superseded by NRM2 in 2013; it applies only where a contract expressly retains it, not as the default BOQ rules.
distractorExplanations.b: CESMM applies to civil engineering, not building BOQ under NRM2.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: UK building BOQs for tender typically follow NRM2 measurement rules. SMM7 legacy references apply only where the contract specifies them.

options.a: Measure to the 1.2m depth band and value the extra depth later as a variation
options.b: Amend description and measure additional depth/rock as separate items
options.c: Cover rock excavation in preliminaries as a time-related contractor risk item
options.d: Keep the description and price rock through dayworks once it is encountered on site

distractorExplanations.a: Known site conditions should be reflected at tender; deferring known extra depth to variations misstates scope and invites claims.
distractorExplanations.c: Rock excavation is measured work, not a time-related preliminary; it should be identified as a separate item or provisional sum.
distractorExplanations.d: Dayworks are a fallback for unforeseen instructed work; rock that is already known should be measured or covered at tender.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: BOQ preparation must align descriptions and quantities with site and design information. Rock may instead be covered by a provisional sum depending on tender strategy.

options.a: Linear metres of slab bearing, stating unit width and span
options.b: Number of units, stating unit length, width, and depth
options.c: Square metres stating thickness, noting structural screed and topping separately
options.d: Cubic metres of concrete, stating strength class, unit depth, and mesh reinforcement

distractorExplanations.a: Bearing length is a detail of the slab, not its measurement unit; hollowcore floors are measured by area with thickness stated.
distractorExplanations.b: Enumerating planks is a supplier's schedule; NRM2 measures precast floor slabs by area in m² stating the thickness.
distractorExplanations.d: Volume measurement applies to in situ concrete; precast hollowcore units are measured in m² with thickness stated.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: NRM2 sets unit conventions for precast flooring and associated notes. Screed and topping are noted separately where applicable.

options.a: Price the BOQ quantity without review to save time
options.b: Add 15% to the concrete rates so the tender total reflects the estimator's own take-off
options.c: Substitute the take-off quantity in the BOQ and price the revised figure without notifying
options.d: Reconcile differences against drawings, NRM2 rules, and query ambiguities before pricing

distractorExplanations.b: Inflating rates to offset a quantity difference distorts the rates used for variations; the variance should be reconciled and queried.
distractorExplanations.c: Tenderers must not alter BOQ quantities unilaterally; discrepancies are raised as tender queries so all bidders price the same basis.
distractorExplanations.a: Pricing should follow reconciled quantities or qualified assumptions.

options.a: NRM1 structures cost planning elements; NRM2 provides detailed measurement for pricing
options.b: NRM1 sets the measurement rules for the tender BOQ; NRM2 governs the order of cost estimate
options.c: NRM2 governs post-contract remeasurement only; NRM1 elements are reused as the tender bills
options.d: They are identical documents with different names

distractorExplanations.b: Swaps the two volumes: NRM1 covers estimating and elemental cost planning, NRM2 the detailed measurement for the tender BOQ.
distractorExplanations.c: NRM2 is used to prepare the tender BOQ, not only post-contract; NRM1 elements are a cost planning structure, not tender bills.
distractorExplanations.d: NRM1 is elemental cost planning; NRM2 is detailed measurement.

options.a: Spread the PS value across the measured rates so the sum is recovered whether or not spent
options.b: Include only attendance/mark-up unless tender documents invite lump-sum pricing of the PS
options.c: Price the PS value as a fixed lump sum, carrying the risk of any overrun on façade access
options.d: Leave the PS out of the tender total, as provisional sums are added when the work is instructed

distractorExplanations.a: Provisional sums are adjusted to actual cost under the contract; loading them into measured rates distorts rates and double counts.
distractorExplanations.c: A provisional sum is not a fixed price risk for the contractor; it is expended or adjusted per instructions and contract rules.
distractorExplanations.d: Provisional sums are stated in the BOQ and carried into the tender total; they are adjusted later, not added on instruction.

options.a: Installation labour risk, as the PC sum fixes the supply price
options.b: Attendance and profit on the fittings, with supply price risk on the contractor
options.c: Difference between PC allowance and actual supply cost
options.d: Inflation on the fittings, with supply cost overruns carried by the contractor

distractorExplanations.a: A PC sum is an allowance, not a fixed price; the employer carries the difference between the allowance and the actual supply cost.
distractorExplanations.d: Under a PC sum the employer carries the full supply cost difference, not just inflation; the contractor prices attendance and profit.
distractorExplanations.b: Swaps the parties: the contractor prices attendance and profit, while the employer carries the supply price difference on PC items.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: PC sums allocate supply cost risk to the employer with contractor attendance. Contractor attendance is adjusted alongside the actual supply cost.

options.a: Stud framing area only, with plasterboard linings measured under painting and decorating
options.b: Partition length in linear metres stating height band, with boarding as a separate m² item
options.c: Net area after deducting every door, borrowed-light, and service opening, however small the void
options.d: Partition area measured face to face including openings unless rules state deduction thresholds

distractorExplanations.a: Boarding is part of the partition construction measured with it; decorations are a separate work section, not where linings go.
distractorExplanations.b: NRM2 measures stud partitions by area; linear measurement by height band is not the default rule for this partition type.
distractorExplanations.c: NRM2 deducts openings only above the stated threshold; deducting every void, however small, departs from the measurement rules.

options.a: Price against defined activities/milestones with scope references
options.b: Remeasure each activity monthly against BOQ quantities at the tendered rates
options.c: Price trade bills to NRM2 and add a fee percentage as under NEC Option E
options.d: Keep the NRM2 bill and convert each bill section total into a single activity

distractorExplanations.b: Remeasuring against quantities is a bill of quantities approach; an activity schedule is paid on completion of defined activities.
distractorExplanations.c: Option E is cost reimbursable with a fee; it does not describe pricing against an activity schedule with scope references.
distractorExplanations.d: Converting bill sections keeps BOQ measurement logic; Option A activities are defined around the programme and Scope, not bill sections.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Option A is priced on an activity schedule: defined activities or milestones linked to the Scope, paid as each activity is completed. Option B remeasures a bill of quantities, so the quantification focus moves from measured items to activity pricing.
mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.prompt: The client switches a tender from NEC4 Option B to Option A, so the priced document becomes an activity schedule instead of a bill of quantities. What quantification focus changes?

options.a: Measure the 1,250 m² drawing area and let the contractor's rate absorb the shortfall
options.b: Adjust quantity to workable area per drawings and site constraints
options.c: Take the drawing area less 10% as a standard allowance for boundary reductions
options.d: Leave paving unmeasured as provisional sum

distractorExplanations.a: Measuring area that cannot be built overstates scope; quantities should reflect the constructible area, not rely on rates.
distractorExplanations.c: A blanket percentage has no measured basis; the quantity should be measured to the actual workable area with assumptions noted.
distractorExplanations.d: Defined paving scope should be measured where information allows.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Measurement must reflect constructible scope with queries for ambiguities. Note any assumption and raise a query if the boundary is unclear.

options.a: Detailed measurement of building works for tender bills of quantities on new-build projects
options.b: Order of cost estimates and cost plans for new-build capital works at RIBA Stages 0–4
options.c: Order of cost estimates and elemental cost planning for building maintenance works
options.d: Measuring NIA and IPMS floor areas for apportioning the shopping centre's service charge

distractorExplanations.a: That describes NRM2 detailed measurement for new-build tender BOQs; NRM3 covers maintenance cost estimating and planning.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses NRM3 with NRM1, which covers capital cost estimating and planning; NRM3 applies the approach to maintenance works.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses NRM3 with the RICS floor measurement standards (IPMS / Code of Measuring Practice); NRM3 covers maintenance cost planning.

options.a: Formwork should be priced in preliminaries as temporary works rather than measured
options.b: Formwork is deemed included in concrete under NRM2, so the combined foundation item is correct
options.c: Formwork should be measured in m³ alongside the concrete rather than by contact area in m²
options.d: Combined items reduce tender transparency and comparability — split per NRM2 where possible

distractorExplanations.a: Formwork to foundations is a measured NRM2 item, not a preliminaries cost; the issue is that lumping hides its cost.
distractorExplanations.b: NRM2 measures formwork separately from concrete supply and placing; it is not deemed included in the concrete item.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses the wrong unit and keeps the items combined; NRM2 measures formwork separately by contact area, not by concrete volume.

options.a: Value using contract rates for similar items or fair rates with quantity per variation rules
options.b: Value at dayworks, since additional doors are not of similar character to BOQ door items
options.c: Value at current market rates, as tender rates lapse once a variation is instructed
options.d: Value at BOQ door rates with no adjustment, even where the extra doors change site conditions

distractorExplanations.b: Extra doors of the same type are of similar character; contract rates apply and dayworks is only a fallback where rates cannot.
distractorExplanations.c: Tender rates do not lapse on instruction; JCT valuation rules use contract rates for similar work under similar conditions.
distractorExplanations.d: Where conditions or quantities change significantly the rates should be fairly adjusted; unadjusted rates are not the rule.

options.a: Firm quantities scaled from the schematics, with design development risk on the subcontractor
options.b: Use provisional quantities or provisional sums with remeasurement mechanism
options.c: A lump sum from £/m² GIA benchmarks, with no quantities until Stage 5 design is issued
options.d: Copy BOQ from a hospital project unchanged

distractorExplanations.a: Schematic drawings cannot support firm quantities; pushing design development risk onto the subcontractor inflates pricing.
distractorExplanations.c: A benchmark lump sum is a cost plan tool, not a subcontract BOQ; provisional quantities give a remeasurable pricing basis.
distractorExplanations.d: BOQs must reflect project-specific design and scope.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Immature MEP design requires provisional quantities/sums and remeasurement provisions. Define how design development will be handled.

options.a: Provisional sums for undefined work such as statutory undertakers' connections
options.b: Client's design team fees and the employer's risk allowance from the cost plan
options.c: Site management, temporary services, hoarding, and insurances
options.d: Daywork allowances for labour, materials and plant with RICS percentage additions

distractorExplanations.a: Provisional sums sit in their own section of the BOQ or summary, not in the preliminaries bill with site setup costs.
distractorExplanations.b: Consultant fees and employer contingency are client costs outside the contractor's BOQ, not preliminaries items.
distractorExplanations.d: Dayworks sit in their own provisional dayworks section of the BOQ; they are not preliminaries site setup and management costs.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Preliminaries cover contractor site-specific setup and management costs. Insurances included are those specific to preliminaries.

options.a: Quantity error risk passes to the contractor, as fixed quantities turn the BOQ into a lump sum
options.b: Quantities become approximate, so the whole contract converts to a remeasurement basis
options.c: Design changes are valued only through dayworks, as fixed quantities cannot be remeasured
options.d: Tenderers may price risk into rates; employer may carry quantity error risk if design changes

distractorExplanations.a: Fixed quantities do not turn the BOQ into a lump sum; under quantities contracts errors are typically corrected at employer cost.
distractorExplanations.c: Design changes are valued under the variation rules using BOQ rates; fixed quantities do not limit valuation to dayworks.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses firm quantities with approximate quantities; a fixed-quantity BOQ is not remeasured, which is why design change creates the risk.

options.a: Tonnes linked to structural schedules, noting bar type and diameter
options.b: Linear metres of bar from the bending schedules, stating diameter and shape code
options.c: Kilograms per m³ of concrete, included in the concrete rate as an allowance
options.d: Excluded because it is invisible after pour

distractorExplanations.b: Bending schedules give lengths, but NRM2 measures bar reinforcement by weight in tonnes, stated by bar type and diameter.
distractorExplanations.c: kg/m³ is a cost planning ratio; NRM2 measures reinforcement as a separate item in tonnes, not within the concrete rate.
distractorExplanations.d: Reinforcement is a major cost item requiring measurement.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: NRM2 measures reinforcement in tonnes with specification linkage. Waste policy should be stated per the BOQ.

options.a: Measure rail civils to NRM2 so that every package shares one consistent measurement basis
options.b: Apply CESMM4 measurement rules and coordinate interfaces with building NRM2 packages
options.c: Apply SMM7 to the civil package, as CESMM4 is intended for highways and water schemes
options.d: Apply NRM3 to the civil package, as rail track is maintenance-led infrastructure

distractorExplanations.a: NRM2 is for building works; the civil package must follow the contract's CESMM4 rules, with interfaces coordinated.
distractorExplanations.d: NRM3 covers building maintenance cost planning; the rail civil package is measured to CESMM4 as stated in the contract.
distractorExplanations.c: SMM7 was a building standard superseded by NRM2 in 2013, and CESMM4 covers civil engineering works generally, including rail civils.

options.a: Let tenderers price directly from the model, with the BOQ quantities treated as indicative
options.b: Provide a COBie data drop for FM handover at RIBA Stage 6 rather than for tender analysis
options.c: Enable consistent automated quantity extraction and audit trail against model and rules
options.d: Transfer measurement accuracy risk to tenderers once they accept the model quantities

distractorExplanations.a: The structured BOQ fixes a common rule-based quantity basis; treating it as indicative removes tender comparability.
distractorExplanations.d: An electronic BOQ format does not reallocate quantity risk; that depends on the contract, not on the file format.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the tender BOQ with COBie handover data; the CSV BOQ is for checking model take-off and tender comparison at tender stage.

options.a: Deemed included in the outer leaf brickwork item under NRM2
options.b: Measured with the inner leaf blockwork as a composite item
options.c: Covered by a provisional sum until the insulation specification is confirmed
options.d: Measured separately as its own NRM2 item linked to wall build-up

distractorExplanations.a: The item expressly excludes the cavity insulation, and NRM2 measures insulation as its own item, not deemed included.
distractorExplanations.b: Insulation is measured as a separate item linked to the wall build-up, not combined into the inner leaf blockwork item.
distractorExplanations.c: Cavity insulation is defined permanent work to be measured as its own NRM2 item, not held as a provisional sum.

options.a: Compare contract BOQ descriptions, drawings, site records, and variation/clause entitlement
options.b: Refer the disagreement to adjudication under the HGCRA before the final account is agreed
options.c: Remeasure the excavation on site and pay any excess over the BOQ quantity at dayworks rates
options.d: Reject the claim, as BOQ excavation items are deemed to include all depths and ground types

distractorExplanations.b: Adjudication is a dispute remedy; the QS first checks BOQ descriptions, drawings and records to establish entitlement.
distractorExplanations.c: Remeasuring before checking BOQ coverage skips entitlement, and any extra would be valued at contract rates, not dayworks.
distractorExplanations.d: NRM2 excavation items are measured in depth bands and ground types; extra depth or rock outside the description can be a valid claim.

options.a: Describing NRM2 measurement rules, units, and deduction thresholds accurately from the standard
options.b: Leading BOQ production, resolving measurement ambiguities, and pricing logic on a live project
options.c: Measuring BOQ sections under supervision and checking quantities against drawings
options.d: Pricing a BOQ prepared by a colleague using BCIS rates without querying its descriptions

distractorExplanations.a: Explaining the rules is Level 1 knowledge; Level 3 needs reasoned advice and leadership of measurement on a live project.
distractorExplanations.c: Supervised measurement and checking is Level 2 application; Level 3 requires leading production and resolving ambiguities.
distractorExplanations.d: Pricing someone else's BOQ without resolving its descriptions is Level 2 application at best; Level 3 needs leadership and reasoned advice.

options.a: Tender totals become fixed lump sums once awarded, so only the overall tender price needs comparing
options.b: Tenderers must price lower rates, as quantity risk passes wholly to the contractor
options.c: Tenderers may price differently for remeasurement risk; employer should analyse rate build-ups
options.d: Employer cannot award contract with provisional quantities

distractorExplanations.a: Provisional quantities are remeasured, so the totals are not fixed; comparison must focus on rates and their build-ups.
distractorExplanations.b: With remeasurement the employer carries quantity risk; tenderers may load rates for uncertainty rather than lower them.
distractorExplanations.d: JCT contracts commonly use provisional quantities with remeasurement.

options.a: A rate from BCIS elemental analyses for ceilings, applied to the GIA in m²
options.b: A specialist's lump-sum quote for the whole ceiling, with no rate or quantity breakdown
options.c: A rate per m² of ceiling grid, with the tiles priced as a separate enumerated item
options.d: Rate build-up from material, labour, waste, access, and smallworks with measured m² quantity

distractorExplanations.a: BCIS elemental rates suit cost planning; BOQ pricing needs a rate build-up applied to the measured ceiling quantity.
distractorExplanations.b: A lump sum without a rate breakdown cannot price a measured m² item or support valuation of variations later.
distractorExplanations.c: Splits a composite ceiling item and enumerates tiles; the tile-and-grid ceiling is measured and priced as one m² item with a rate build-up.

options.a: Follow contract-stated measurement method and coordinate with FIDIC re-measurement clauses
options.b: Apply RICS POMI by default, as international FIDIC projects override UK practice
options.c: Treat the BOQ as fixed quantities, as the FIDIC Red Book is a lump-sum contract
options.d: Value measured work under JCT SBC valuation rules, as the stated measurement method is UK-based

distractorExplanations.b: The contract states a UK-based method; POMI applies only if the contract adopts it, not by default on FIDIC projects.
distractorExplanations.c: The FIDIC Red Book is a remeasurement contract; quantities are measured and valued under its measurement clauses.
distractorExplanations.d: A UK-based measurement method does not import JCT valuation rules; valuation follows the FIDIC clauses in the contract.

options.a: Measure gross area, deducting openings over 1.0 m², the threshold used for masonry
options.b: Measure gross area and deduct qualifying openings per stated threshold
options.c: Deduct every opening, including voids under 0.5 m², to give the net area
options.d: Measure openings only without wall area

distractorExplanations.a: Applies a 1.0 m² threshold borrowed from another work section; the linings rule stated here deducts voids over 0.5 m².
distractorExplanations.c: Voids below the 0.5 m² threshold are not deducted; deducting every opening departs from the stated NRM2 rule.
distractorExplanations.d: Linings are measured as areas with rule-based deductions.

options.a: Inflation between the cost plan base date and BOQ preparation altering the area
options.b: Cost plan quantities measured to NRM2 rules while the BOQ uses NRM1 elemental rules
options.c: Different measurement boundaries, gross vs net, or BOQ includes features not in cost plan
options.d: Use of different BCIS location factors between the cost plan and the BOQ pricing

distractorExplanations.a: Inflation changes cost, not measured area; a quantity variance points to boundary or gross/net measurement differences.
distractorExplanations.b: Swaps the standards: the cost plan uses NRM1 elemental quantities and the BOQ uses NRM2 detailed measurement.
distractorExplanations.d: Location factors adjust cost, not measured area; an 8% quantity variance points to boundary or gross/net measurement differences.

options.a: Valuation of all variations, replacing BOQ rates even where similar items exist
options.b: Pricing provisional sums at tender, with percentages applied to each PS value
options.c: Valuing time-related preliminaries during extensions of time on the project
options.d: Valuation of instructed work without prior rates using daywork percentages

distractorExplanations.a: Daywork is a fallback where work cannot be measured; BOQ rates take precedence where similar items exist.
distractorExplanations.b: Daywork percentages value instructed work post-contract; they are not used to price provisional sums at tender.
distractorExplanations.c: Extended preliminaries are valued from the time-related prelims build-up, not from the daywork schedule.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Daywork schedules provide fallback valuation basis for certain instructed works. Percentages are applied to labour, plant and materials.

options.a: Area of cladding panels in m² stating system type and performance
options.b: Number of panels by type, stating panel size and glazing specification
options.c: Linear metres of mullions and transoms, with glazing as a separate m² item
options.d: Girth of the façade in linear metres, stating storey height and system type

distractorExplanations.b: Enumerating panels is a fabricator's schedule; NRM2 measures curtain walling by area in m² with system described.
distractorExplanations.c: Curtain walling is measured as a complete system by area, not split into linear framing and separate glazing.
distractorExplanations.d: Uses a linear unit for a panelised system; NRM2 measures curtain walling by area in m² with system type and performance stated.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Curtain wall BOQ items use m² with performance and system descriptors. Excluded adjacent works should be stated.

options.a: Answer the subcontractor's query directly by email, leaving other tenderers to raise their own queries
options.b: Issue clarification/amendment via tender query process with consistent addendum to all tenderers
options.c: Ask the tenderer to state its own scope assumption as a qualification to its bid
options.d: Omit item 3.14 from the tender comparison and instruct it later as a variation once agreed

distractorExplanations.a: A private answer gives one tenderer different information; clarifications must go to all tenderers by addendum.
distractorExplanations.c: Qualifications on an ambiguous item make bids non-comparable; the QS should clarify the item for all tenderers.
distractorExplanations.d: Leaving an ambiguous item out of the tender converts known scope into a post-contract variation; it should be clarified for every tenderer.

options.a: Based on the contractor's claimed percentage complete applied to each BOQ item total in the application
options.b: Taken from the contractor's own dimension sheets unchecked, with verification deferred to final account
options.c: Measured to date per contract rules with substantiated dimension sheets and audit trail
options.d: Taken from tender BOQ quantities pro rata to the programme time elapsed

distractorExplanations.a: Percentage complete suits lump-sum valuations; a remeasurement contract values quantities actually measured to date.
distractorExplanations.d: Time elapsed does not measure work done; remeasurement valuations rely on substantiated measured quantities.
distractorExplanations.b: Interim remeasurement needs verified quantities each period; deferring checks to final account risks overpayment during the works.

options.a: Ancillary components are covered by a provisional sum until their extent is known
options.b: Ancillary items are paid at dayworks rates when instructed by the contract administrator
options.c: Ancillary items are measured as separate lines so that tenderers can price them individually
options.d: Certain ancillary components are included in the main item rate without separate measurement

distractorExplanations.a: Deemed included items are priced within the main item rate, not held as a provisional sum for later adjustment.
distractorExplanations.b: Deemed included work needs no instruction or separate payment; it is already covered by the measured item rate.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the rule: deemed included ancillaries are not measured separately but priced within the main item rate.

options.a: Validate model LOD, exclusions, connections, and NRM2/grouping before accepting quantities
options.b: Accept model quantities once the federated model has passed clash detection at the Stage 4 design review
options.c: Check model tonnage against BCIS kg/m² benchmarks and accept if within range
options.d: Accept quantities exported via IFC, as model data at LOD 300 is measured to NRM2 by default

distractorExplanations.b: Clash detection checks coordination, not measurement; LOD, exclusions and NRM2 grouping still need QS validation.
distractorExplanations.c: A benchmark ratio is a cost planning sense check; it does not validate connections, exclusions or measurement rules.
distractorExplanations.d: IFC export and LOD describe geometry and data detail, not measurement rules; the QS must still check exclusions, connections and NRM2 grouping.

options.a: Contingency covers defined work not yet designed; PS cover unforeseen project risks
options.b: Contingency is employer risk allowance; PS are contract items for defined scope
options.c: PS sit in the cost plan only, while contingency is priced by tenderers in the BOQ
options.d: Contingency is a contractor risk allowance carried within the preliminaries bill

distractorExplanations.a: Swaps the two: contingency is the employer's risk allowance, while provisional sums are contract items for identified work.
distractorExplanations.c: Provisional sums are contract items in the BOQ, whereas contingency is usually an employer allowance outside the tender.
distractorExplanations.d: The cost plan contingency is the employer's risk allowance, not a contractor's preliminaries item in the BOQ.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Distinguishing contingency from provisional sums is essential costing practice. Contingency is often not included in the tender BOQ.

options.a: Structural demolition by volume, with soft strip and propping in preliminaries
options.b: Demolition by gross floor area, with asbestos removal excluded as client's risk
options.c: Soft strip, structural demolition, temporary propping, and waste disposal
options.d: Structural demolition and waste disposal, with soft strip carried in the fit-out package

distractorExplanations.a: Soft strip and temporary propping are measured demolition items, not preliminaries, and must be quantified separately.
distractorExplanations.b: Hazardous material removal still needs a scope allowance or provisional sum; excluding it leaves a major cost unrecorded.
distractorExplanations.d: Soft strip is part of the demolition scope and precedes structural demolition; moving it to fit-out also omits temporary propping.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Urban demolition BOQs include method, protection, and disposal components. Neighbour protection should also be captured.

options.a: Submit on the original BOQ and note the addendum as a qualification to the tender
options.b: Ask for a tender period extension and hold the bid until earthworks are remeasured on site
options.c: Price the original quantities, as the employer will remeasure earthworks post-contract
options.d: Reprice or confirm rates remain valid for adjusted quantities per tender instructions

distractorExplanations.a: Addenda form part of the tender documents; tenderers must price the revised quantities, not qualify against them.
distractorExplanations.c: Remeasurement later does not excuse ignoring the addendum; tenders must be priced on the issued revised quantities.
distractorExplanations.b: Remeasurement happens post-contract; the addendum quantities must be priced or confirmed within the tender period as instructed.

options.a: Strength class, exposure, pour size, and whether reinforcement is excluded
options.b: Strength class only, with exposure and pour size left to the supplier's discretion
options.c: Ready-mix supplier, delivery distance, and pump hire for each foundation pour
options.d: Architect's favourite mix code without specification

distractorExplanations.b: Exposure class and pour size materially affect mix and placing cost; the rate description must define them.
distractorExplanations.c: These are the estimator's pricing inputs, not the specification items a BOQ unit rate description should clarify.
distractorExplanations.d: Rates must tie to defined specification and measurement rules.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Clear BOQ descriptions enable comparable concrete rate pricing. The formwork interface should also be clear.

options.a: Employer issues a firm NRM2 BOQ and the contractor prices it as under JCT SBC
options.b: Employer documents define performance scope; contractor quantifies completed design in tender
options.c: Employer measures the contractor's proposals post-contract and remeasures at completion
options.d: Employer prepares an NRM1 elemental cost plan that becomes the contract sum analysis

distractorExplanations.a: A firm employer BOQ is a traditional SBC approach; in D&B the contractor quantifies its own completed design.
distractorExplanations.c: D&B is normally a lump sum on the contractor's proposals; the employer does not remeasure the design post-contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Swaps the parties: in D&B the contractor prepares the contract sum analysis from its own proposals; the employer's cost plan stays internal.

options.a: A fixed lump sum for set-up and removal, independent of the contract period
options.b: A percentage of the measured works value, adjusted at final account for any change in contract duration
options.c: Weekly/monthly rates for staff and plant with estimated duration linked to programme
options.d: Identical prelims on 6-week and 80-week projects

distractorExplanations.a: That describes fixed-charge preliminaries such as set-up; time-related charges vary with programme duration.
distractorExplanations.b: A percentage proxy is not a substantive build-up; time-related prelims are priced as periodic rates times duration.
distractorExplanations.d: Duration strongly affects time-related preliminary costs.

options.a: Single 'item' for reception joinery, with scope defined by the specification only
options.b: Linear metres of reception counter, with panelling in m² and no drawing reference
options.c: A provisional sum for reception joinery until the fit-out designer finalises details
options.d: Detailed item description with nr count, dimensions, materials, and drawing reference

distractorExplanations.a: A single item without enumeration or dimensions gives tenderers no comparable basis; joinery should be described and counted.
distractorExplanations.b: Bespoke joinery units are enumerated with dimensions and drawing references; unreferenced linear items risk scope gaps.
distractorExplanations.c: Reception joinery is designed scope that can be enumerated and described; a provisional sum gives tenderers no comparable basis.

options.a: Duplications, gaps at interfaces, and coordinated provisional allowances
options.b: Differences in unit rates between the two disciplines' tender returns
options.c: Consistency of preliminaries between the M&E and main contract packages
options.d: Variances between each BOQ total and its cost plan element allowance

distractorExplanations.b: Rate comparison is tender analysis; the interface cross-check is about duplicated or missing scope between BOQs.
distractorExplanations.c: Preliminaries alignment is a separate check; the cross-check targets duplications and gaps at scope interfaces.
distractorExplanations.d: Cost plan reconciliation is a separate budget check; the cross-discipline review targets duplicated or missing scope at interfaces.

options.a: Measured into the BOQ quantities under NRM2, so rates exclude any waste factor
options.b: Applied per material type and site constraints with stated percentage in build-up
options.c: A single 5% uplift on the tender total to cover material waste
options.d: Included in the preliminaries bill as a time-related site management cost

distractorExplanations.a: NRM2 measures net quantities as fixed; waste is allowed for in the rate build-up, not added to measured quantities.
distractorExplanations.c: Waste varies by material and method; a flat uplift on the total ignores material-specific waste in rate build-ups.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses material waste factors with preliminaries such as skips; waste allowances belong in each material's rate build-up.

options.a: Uniclass replaces NRM2 as the rule set for measuring the BOQ quantities
options.b: Uniclass codes are applied at handover in the asset register rather than in the BOQ
options.c: Structure items with Uniclass codes for lifecycle costing and FM integration
options.d: Use Uniclass in place of COBie, as it replaces the FM data exchange at handover

distractorExplanations.a: Uniclass is a classification system; measurement still follows NRM2, with Uniclass codes added to the items.
distractorExplanations.b: The employer asked for a Uniclass-aligned BOQ; coding at the BOQ stage is what links cost data to lifecycle FM.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a classification system with a data exchange format; Uniclass codes are carried within COBie, not a substitute for it.

options.a: Repeating main contract BOQ descriptions, as subcontract BOQs should use trade shorthand
options.b: Including main contract quantities, as subcontractors should remeasure from drawings
options.c: Passing down the main contract measurement rules, as subcontracts should use trade norms
options.d: Scope gaps at interfaces and inconsistent measurement rules between main and sub BOQs

distractorExplanations.a: Main contract descriptions carry agreed scope; shortening them to trade shorthand creates the scope gaps to avoid.
distractorExplanations.b: Sharing consistent quantities helps alignment; the risk is gaps and inconsistent measurement rules, not the quantities.
distractorExplanations.c: Consistent measurement rules between main and sub BOQs are what prevent gaps; switching to trade norms creates the mismatch to avoid.

options.a: Pile type, diameter, depth criteria, testing regime, and ground conditions interface
options.b: Pile cap dimensions, reinforcement cages, and blinding to the pile caps below slab
options.c: Rig mobilisation, piling mat, and arisings disposal as preliminaries items only
options.d: Test loads set equal to the 800kN working load, with pile length left to the contractor

distractorExplanations.b: Pile caps are substructure items after piling; the working load check concerns pile type, depth, testing and ground.
distractorExplanations.c: These are piling preliminaries and enabling items; they do not verify the pile design parameters behind 800kN.
distractorExplanations.d: Proof test loads normally exceed working load, and depth criteria must be verified against ground conditions, not left open.

options.a: How the BOQ was measured to NRM2, leaving rate build-up to the estimating team
options.b: How quantities, market rates, labour/plant, risk, and prelims combined into tender pricing
options.c: How your tender compared with the other bidders' totals and with the client's pre-tender estimate
options.d: That pricing is confidential and cannot be discussed

distractorExplanations.a: Describing measurement alone omits pricing logic; Level 3 needs your own reasoning on rates, risk and prelims.
distractorExplanations.c: Comparing totals is tender analysis outcome; assessors probe how the price was built up and the judgments made.
distractorExplanations.d: Candidates must articulate pricing approach at interview.

options.a: Membrane area only, with penetrations and sumps deemed included in the m² rate
options.b: Membrane volume in m³ by thickness, with protection boards in the concrete item
options.c: Surface preparation, membranes, protection boards, and detailing at penetrations
options.d: Membranes and protection boards, with surface preparation left in groundworks

distractorExplanations.a: Penetration and sump detailing is a significant cost and must be measured, not treated as deemed included.
distractorExplanations.d: Surface preparation is part of the tanking scope; leaving it to groundworks risks a gap at the interface.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses the wrong unit and moves scope: membranes are measured by area in m², and protection boards are part of the tanking item.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Waterproofing BOQ scope includes preparation, membranes, and detailing. Include these items as defined in the scope.

options.a: Contractor is paid the tender tonnage, as BOQ errors are its risk
options.b: Tender total stands, with the error corrected only by a variation
options.c: The overstatement is settled by a negotiated lump-sum deduction at final account
options.d: Interim and final valuations use actual measured quantities

distractorExplanations.a: In a remeasurement contract the contractor is paid for steel actually installed, not the overstated tender tonnage.
distractorExplanations.b: Remeasurement adjusts quantities as measured; correction does not depend on issuing a variation instruction.
distractorExplanations.c: A remeasurement contract corrects the error automatically by measuring actual steel at BOQ rates; no negotiated deduction is needed.

mrics-quantity-surveying-readiness-check.explanation: Remeasurement contracts adjust payment to actual quantities at agreed rates. The employer benefits from the rate multiplied by the reduced quantity.

options.a: Separate preliminaries or provisional sums for major temporary works
options.b: Including temporary works in permanent work rates as deemed included items
options.c: Dayworks valued after each temporary works design is approved on site
options.d: Client-designed temporary works issued as a measured bill under NRM2

distractorExplanations.b: Major temporary works should be visible; burying them in permanent rates hides cost and design responsibility.
distractorExplanations.c: Dayworks are a fallback for unmeasurable instructed work, not the planned pricing route for known temporary works.
distractorExplanations.d: Temporary works design responsibility usually sits with the contractor and varies by contract; it is not client design by default.
